newsitem.title: USA: McCormick defends use of exclusivity pacts.
newsitem.headline: McCormick defends use of exclusivity pacts.

text.p: McCormick and Co Inc, the food and spice maker, Thursday defended its exclusivity agreements with its customers, saying those agreements were used in a small number of cases and were "appropriate and not an unfair method of competition."

The company issued the statement as it confirmed that the U.S. Federal Trade Commission was investigating whether its use of exclusivity clauses in certain customer contracts constituted unfair competition.
Robert Lawless, president of the company, said McCormick "takes pride in conducting its business honestly and ethically."
"We firmly believe that we have not engaged in any unethical marketing practices," he said, adding that reports suggesting the contrary were "absolutely outrageous, unfounded and offensive."
In a statement, McCormick said it had not prevously reported its use of exclusivity clauses "because it is immaterial."
It said federal regulators have made no determination that the clauses constitute an unfair practice and that there are no claims for damages, whether punitive or otherwise, against McCormick.

In a report on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal quoted a Prudential Securities analyst, John McMillin, as saying that news of the investigation surfaced in an analysts' conference call earlier this week with Australia's Burns, Philp & Co, which is a McCormick competitor.

McMillin had said, according to the account, that Burns Philp officials stated at the conference call that the FTC had sought information from the Australian company as part of the McCormick investigation.
